I tested Amazon’s cheapest soundbar and it delivers exceptionally clear dialogue and surprisingly competent bass for a really low price

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1431 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is a supremely affordable soundbar that doesn’t compromise on performance.
  • Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you.
  • Price: 5/5Sound quality: 4.5/5Design: 4/5Features: 5/5Overall score: 4.5/5Best for: Upgraders on a budget.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is a supremely affordable soundbar that doesn’t compromise on performance. It’s easily one of the best bang-for-buck soundbars I’ve ever tested, and at $119, I can’t quite believe the price.

Some bass-heavy scenes can push dialogue back.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Price: 5/5Sound quality: 4.5/5Design: 4/5Features: 5/5Overall score: 4.5/5Best for: Upgraders on a budget.

According to recent reports, when a soundbar is this cheap, it can feel too good to be true. With an MSRP os $119, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar definitely falls into that category. How can it be one of the best soundbars when it costs less than a monthly cellphone subscription?

According to recent reports, the answer is: I’m not sure. I genuinely doubt Amazon is making a profit on this soundbar.

For something this inexpensive, bass is surprisingly competent, and it has a dedicated dialogue mode on top of two EQs for music and movies. I never struggled to make out dialogue, even in action-heavy scenes, which is something the TV Soundbar’s significant brother, the TV Soundbar Plus, struggled with.

Sources indicate that so, might the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar be the budget model for you? To find out, keep reading this Amazon Fire TV Soundbar review.

24 inches x 2.5 inches x 3.5 inches.

The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar has a lot going for it: namely its supremely affordable MSRP and surprisingly deft sound.

Industry observers note that the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is $119 at Amazon U.S. and £119 at Amazon U.K. — this is incredibly cheap for a soundbar, let alone a soundbar that sounds this good. And, it's down to $74 for Black Friday.

I’ve also tested the $67 Majority Naga 60 and the $119 Sony HT-S100F, but I’d recommend the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar over both of these due to its superior bass.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, now, let’s get one thing straight. The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar will not, and does not, sound like its more expensive brethren. Want Sonos Ray ($219) or Bose TV Speaker 2nd Gen ($299) quality? It’s not here.

However, this is an $119 soundbar. That’s it. For the price of a monthly cellphone bill, you get a soundbar. And while it doesn’t have the same detail or controlled bass you’d expect on a premium model, that’s okay. That’s not what the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is, and that’s fine.

Even so, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar still sounds better than TV speakers — and that’s all it’s trying to be.

I always test soundbars with 4K Blu-rays, basic-tier Netflix, and music via Bluetooth or AirPlay (connectivity dependent). To test the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar, I watched “Top Gun: Maverick,” “K-Pop Demon Hunters” and “The Batman” on 4K Blu-ray.

In a recent development, “Top Gun: Maverick”’is opening scene is a goldmine for speaker testing. There are all these different sounds fighting for attention: the iconic pulsing bassline in “Danger Zone,” high-frequency in-scene effects like whooshing ropes and clinking metal, and overpowering sounds like jet engines taking off.

I could hear the propulsive bass in “Danger Zone,” which didn’t overpower the jet engines. While there was a little tinniness at the top of the high-end, I really didn’t mind this in the grand scheme of things. The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar performed admirably.

Dialogue was also clear, even in radioed dialogue scenes. While deep voices, like Tom Cruise’s, caused a little rumbling, I could still understand all dialogue.

“KPop Demon Hunters” also sounded strong: despite a little tinniness in some of the in-movie songs’ percussion, dialogue was particularly exceptional. Bass in the soundtrack was powerful, and diegetic sounds like slamming doors came through well.

Industry observers note that afterwards, I watched “The Batman,” which is a challenging movie for soundbars thanks to the moody dialogue and near-constant rainfall. I could hear every word muttered (yes, muttered; that’s how everyone speaks in this movie). Even footsteps across rainy concrete came through clearly.

In a recent development, however, loud scenes — like the club scene — pushed dialogue to the back and overpowered the in-scene electronic music, which meant I strained to hear a few of the Penguin’s words. However, I didn’t experience this in any other movie. It’s a Batman thing.

I was extremely surprised and intrigued by this sound quality. It’s miles better than I thought it would be.

The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar has a range of EQ modes: dialogue, movie, music, and you can individually adjust bass. I had to cycle through the EQs to activate each EQ.

Sources indicate that however, the EQs actually improved my viewing experience. I switched between “dialogue” and “movie” while watching “Top Gun”; movie increased bass; dialogue — ever-so surprisingly — clarified dialogue. Music made speech a little too sharp, but obviously, watching a movie in “music” mode is very much "play stupid games, win stupid prizes".

Industry observers note that you can even listen to music via Bluetooth, but I wouldn’t write home about this. It would do in a pinch, but the percussion was tinny and the soundbar narrowed the soundstage. It’s fine, but I would just listen to music on one of the best speakers, like the JBL Flip 7.

It’s great to have these options on such a budget-friendly soundbar.

There’s very little I dislike about this soundbar, hence the 4.5-star rating.

In a recent development, I feel almost unfair marking this as a con, but Amazon kind of brought it upon itself by giving the soundbar DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio. There is no Dolby Atmos or any kind of surround sound. You only really find DTS Virtual:X on select DVDs, so you’ll need to ensure you buy compatible discs to really benefit from this.

Dolby Atmos content — like premium Netflix or Disney+ — will not play as true surround sound because the soundbar is physically incapable of it. If you want spatial audio, you'll have to go for the slightly more expensive Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus.

This is an incredibly cheap soundbar. I really don’t know how Amazon is making a profit on it, if it is at all. At $119, there’s really not much competition.

The only soundbar that comes close is the $119 Sony HT-S100F, which is one of the best cheap soundbars on the market. However, the Sony’s bass is a little lackluster. While the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar’s bass can be a little rumbly at times, at least it isn’t lackluster. What you prefer will depend on you.

In terms of similarly priced competition… well, that’s kind of it. I’ve also tested the Majority Naga 60, which is incredibly cheap at $67, but it can suffer from pinchy treble and rattling bass.

In a recent development, if you want better-than-TV-speaker sound on a serious budget, there’s only one answer to this question: Yes. Actually, wait, I’ve just thought of another: Heck yes.

It has been revealed that I was extremely surprised by the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar’s sound, and I’m sure you will be, too. After testing some disappointing and overpriced Amazon Fire Ember TVs, I wasn’t expecting much — but the soundbar completely blew me away. It’s room-filling, mostly well-controlled, and has extremely intelligible dialogue.

Recent findings suggest that it's much better than the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus ($139 on Amazon), whose built-in subwoofer overpowers dialogue in action-heavy scenes. If you have a little more to spend, you might want to look into the Amazon Fire TV Plus with Subwoofer ($229) or the model with Rears ($349).

It has been revealed that however, for those on a serious budget, this is the best option out there. Hands-down.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • Recent findings suggest that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • Industry observers note that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what customers need to know.

Recent findings suggest that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

Industry observers note that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly claims it has no looks for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft aims to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Sources indicate that planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the organization.

The June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

In a recent development, microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

Sources indicate that “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team aims. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

United Airlines Has Warned Air Traffic Control Isn’t Ready for Air Taxis. That’s a Bigger Problem for Archer Than Its Cash Burn.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been a rough couple of weeks for air travel and for airlines, especially for United Airlines (UAL -4.26%).
  • While this wasn't good news for United and other airline stocks, the technical difficulties in air traffic are a real problem for Archer Aviation (ACHR -9.06%) and other companies focusing on air taxis, commonly known as electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft.
  • Last spring, United CEO Scott Kirby expressed concerns about whether the nation's air traffic control system was ready for eVTOLs, and the recent ground stop led him to say the FAA needs to invest more in updating its technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Halley – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:05PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Archer Aviation ›.

It has been a rough couple of weeks for air travel and for airlines, especially for United Airlines (UAL -4.26%). The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) imposed a nationwide ground stop on Friday, leading to delays and cancellations after a newly installed router malfunctioned. Then, United had its own issues on Monday, with a 90-minute system outage that caused delays.

While this wasn't good news for United and other airline stocks, the technical difficulties in air traffic are a real problem for Archer Aviation (ACHR -9.06%) and other companies focusing on air taxis, commonly known as electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft.

Last spring, United CEO Scott Kirby expressed concerns about whether the nation's air traffic control system was ready for eVTOLs, and the recent ground stop led him to say the FAA needs to invest more in updating its technology.

Neither the FAA's nor United's technical problems reflect a flaw in Archer's Midnight aircraft itself, nor do they threaten Archer's cash runway or manufacturing ramp-up.

In a recent development, EVTOL commercialization is heavily dependent on ecosystem readiness, certified airspace rules from the FAA, and seamless hub-and-app execution from United and other airlines. The recent tech issues raise the risk of delays in Archer's transition from flight testing to full-scale commercial passenger service in the U.S.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that archer's shares are down more than 52% so far this year. Investors have been concerned about the firm's massive losses and high cash burn. In the third quarter, the company had $5.1 million in revenue, which was progress, because it had no revenue in the same period a year ago. However, it also lost $274.6 million, more than double the $129.9 million it lost in the third quarter of 2025.

The firm's spending is ramping up as it begins production at its manufacturing facility in Covington, Georgia. To start generating more revenue, the company depends on FAA authorization, and the agency's issues hurt Archer.

Archer's Midnight eVTOL aircraft relies on the FAA for Type certification and National Airspace System (NAS) integration; any internal technical bottlenecks at the regulator trickle down to Archer.

The FAA's complications with aging IT infrastructure, staffing shortages, and system outages may lead it to divert engineering and IT resources toward stabilizing legacy commercial aviation systems and bandwidth for emerging technologies, and put eVTOL operational rules and reviews of Archer's final Phase 4 Type Certification flight test data on the back burner.

In a recent development, archer's business model depends on high-frequency, short-haul urban air-taxi routes, such as those from Manhattan to Newark. Integrating autonomous or semiautomated eVTOLs into congested Class B airspace requires modernized FAA data-sharing and traffic management software. Delays in the FAA's NextGen and digital traffic-management upgrades limit how quickly Archer can scale beyond initial, low-volume visual flight rules (VFR) corridors.

If nothing else, the high-profile technical failures could make regulators more risk-averse, leading to stricter software validation and redundancy requirements for new aircraft entrants.

Industry observers note that united Airlines is Archer's most vital commercial partner, strategic investor, and launch customer, with a conditional order book of up to $1.5 billion for 200 Midnight aircraft, plus an option for 100 more. United's recent tech and operational hiccups affect Archer in three ways:.

Archer continues to ramp up flight testing of its Midnight eVTOLs. The technology makes sense, particularly in crowded urban markets. However, the company is entering uncharted airspace, so to speak, and the FAA certification process for eVTOL aircraft is complex and unprecedented. Although progress continues, timeline delays stretch out the horizon before commercial passenger routes can officially launch.

Sources indicate that each delayed phase lengthens the window during which Archer must burn through hundreds of millions of dollars without commercial passenger inflows. That makes Archer a risky stock for most investors.

Halide 3.4 is out today as the latest enhancement to the pro camera app. The update adds several new features, including a larger viewfinder for iPhone Duo and more.

The new Halide upgrade also lets you use the outer screen on iPhone Duo as a live preview or a fill flash. It brings back a few camera tools from Halide Mark II as well.

Lux Optics first added iPhone Duo support in October with Halide 3.3. With the phone fully open, the initial iPhone Duo upgrade let you review your most recent photo alongside the live viewfinder.

Today’s upcoming XL mode gives you the option to swap the photo preview for a larger viewfinder. Controls on both sides enable two-handed shooting.

While the Duo is open, the outer screen can mirror Halide’s camera controls or show a full-screen viewfinder without controls. The second option lets the person you’re photographing see how you’ve framed the shot.

In low light, Halide can use the outer screen as a fill flash. That gives you a softer source of light for portraits, and Halide’s developers recommend turning the screen brightness all the way up before taking the photo.

Halide also now places the histogram along the Duo’s crease. The revision revises the Photo Lab interface for editing with the Duo half open as well.

On other iPhones, Halide 3.4 restores the color and luminance histograms and the shutter timer from Mark II.

Recent findings suggest that halide Mark III introduced back in May with a redesigned camera and the fresh Photo Lab editor. Recent updates added RAW-only capture in 3.1 and Aperture Priority for iPhone 18 Pro in 3.2. Halide Mark III version 3.4 is available now on the App Store.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of fresh features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.
  • Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).
  • But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of fresh features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a upcoming setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

While wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

Upcoming in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

You can also move the new slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

According to a new report from Bloomberg, Apple’s head of camera and photo software retired last month. Jon McCormack spent eight years at Apple and “oversaw the Camera and Photos apps and the underlying technology that determines how owners capture, view, and edit their pictures and video.”.

In a recent development, 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Mark Gurman reports that Apple hasn’t named a upcoming vice president to replace McCormack, who reported to software chief Craig Federighi. “Instead, his former deputies are assuming his responsibilities under other executives,” the report indicates.

In his role, McCormack oversaw “close coordination between software engineers and Apple’s camera hardware and chip teams.” He’s credited with last year’s redesigned selfie camera and other projects:.

In a recent development, his work included the redesigned selfie camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup last year. This year, Apple added a variable-aperture camera to the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, giving people more control over lighting and depth of field. The organization also introduced a customizable Camera app interface with professional controls.

Bloomberg describes McCormack as a “strong opponent of using generative AI to create or alter photographs,” a philosophy that created tension as Apple embraced AI tools in the Photos app. His retirement, however, “wasn’t related to a disagreement or clash with Apple over its AI strategy,” the report states.

Industry observers note that mcCormack spoke in depth about iOS 27 features like Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing in an interview with Tyler Stalman in June. He emphasized how the features “preserve the integrity of the moment.”.

What we learned operating auth for 1k APIs

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nango

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in May 2025, we merged a PR at Nango that had a critical bug: an if condition that never fired prevented refreshed credentials from being saved to the database.
  • In those two hours, our scheduled jobs had refreshed and discarded access and refresh tokens for hundreds of connections.
  • Then we learned how many providers rotate refresh tokens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in May 2025, we merged a PR at Nango that had a critical bug: an if condition that never fired prevented refreshed credentials from being saved to the database. We caught the bug and reverted it in just under two hours.

In those two hours, our scheduled jobs had refreshed and discarded access and refresh tokens for hundreds of connections. For most APIs, that was recoverable: the old refresh token still worked, so the next scheduled refresh repaired the connection.

Then we learned how many providers rotate refresh tokens.

Many providers, including Airtable and Atlassian, invalidate the old refresh token the moment a replacement is issued. Salesforce and Slack can do the same when rotation is enabled for the OAuth app.

It has been revealed that there was no way to get those tokens back. For every affected connection, our customers had to ask their owners to go through the consent screen again.

OAuth is a standard, but OAuth providers are not interchangeable. Each APIâs auth behaves a little differently, and some of those differences are undocumented and only surface in production.

According to recent reports, for context, Nango is an open-source project that lets web applications and agents integrate with third-party APIs. Our customers embed it in their products. Their users connect third-party accounts, and Nango keeps those connections working.

Since then, weâve grown from supporting about 400 APIs to 1,000+ APIs. The incident changed how we operate auth, but it was only the first of several lessons.

Recent findings suggest that refresh token rotation is a security win, but a bug in the rotation path can permanently destroy a connection and force the user to reauthorize. Thatâs what made our incident so expensive.

Sources indicate that we now treat refresh tokens like money, not cache. The new token gets persisted before anything else can fail. The persistence path has its own regression tests, and any platform-level refresh anomalies immediately page the on-call team.

In a recent development, take Airtable: a refresh request with a stale token or the wrong client credentials can return a 400 or 401, but Airtable doesnât stop there. It revokes the userâs entire authorization for your app, and the only way back is for the user to reconnect. Sending the same refresh request twice can also cause revocation. Airtable documents a short grace period for duplicate refreshes, but retrying the stale token after that period revokes the authorization.

Airtable also invalidates the old access token the instant a refresh succeeds, so a long-running job still using an old token can fail mid-run.

Xero handles it better: if a refresh fails or the response never arrives, you can retry with the previous refresh token for up to 30 minutes.

Issues like these pushed us to serialize refreshes per connection behind a distributed lock.

According to recent reports, *This is only the success path. Failure paths donât fit in one diagram.

Sources indicate that even refreshing early can be wrong. For example, Exact Onlineâs access tokens last for 10 minutes, and its token endpoint rejects any refresh attempt made more than 30 seconds before expiry. Our ârefresh 15 minutes earlyâ rule meant every refresh fell outside that window and was rejected. We had to add support for per-provider expiration buffers.

The official OAuth 2.0 spec (RFC 6749) makes expires_in optional for access tokens. For us, this has been a recurring source of silent breakage.

Zendesk, for example, rolled out expiring access tokens for OAuth clients, including existing ones. Its token response includes expires_in only if you request it. Without that parameter, the access token still expires under the default policy, but the response doesnât say when. We discovered this only after the rotating refresh token lapsed and connections started dying.

In a recent development, salesforceâs token response includes no expiry. The documented way to check it is a separate introspection endpoint, which we call before deciding whether to refresh an access token.

But in June 2024, the introspection endpoint started intermittently returning unsupported_token_type for some tokens. When introspection failed, we refreshed anyway. The replacement access token could be introspected normally, though we never learned why the original token failed.

We now refresh stale credentials on a cron, so tokens get exercised before inactivity kills them.

Recent findings suggest that youâd expect an auth failure to return a 401. It often doesnât:.

We ended up building per-provider heuristics: at the time of this analysis, 276 of the roughly 935 providers in our registry declared an authenticated endpoint that Nango can call to check whether credentials still work.

16% of commits to our provider config are fixes. Thereâs no reliable feed for provider auth changes; we often learn about them from a failed flow or a customer report.

Recent findings suggest that figma unveiled by email that credentials had to move from the request body to a Basic Authorization header and that the OAuth host was changing. We shipped the upgrade, but anyone who missed the email might not discover the change until refreshes begin failing.

Shopify changed how offline tokens are issued, so apps began receiving expiring tokens where they previously didnât. We shipped a config change to preserve the old behavior.

Recent findings suggest that supporting a newly introduced API assumes two things: you can get credentials to test with, and you can find accurate docs for how its auth works. At our scale, both assumptions fail often enough that going around the provider is routine:.

API clients would fail less often if providers did these ten things:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jack Delaney – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:09PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

After nearly every initial public offering (IPO), insiders and pre-IPO stakeholders have to wait for a period before they can sell shares on the open market. These lockup periods can last for up to a year, but their expirations always cause some concern among new shareholders. After all, if insiders flood the market with their shares and demand from buyers doesn't keep up with supply, it can put downward pressure on the stock price.

For Anthropic (ANT -8.50%), which went public on Nov. 19, employees and executives will eventually have the opportunity to sell more of their shares. But instead of lockup periods ending, there are higher priorities for shareholders to focus on.

If employees start selling when a lockup period ends, that shouldn't be viewed as an automatic red flag or a signal that they have lost faith in their tech giant. Rather, it's one of the first times they can turn the paper wealth they've accumulated over the years into actual liquid wealth.

Industry observers note that for Anthropic, the lockup expirations are more staggered than a traditional IPO, with shares unlocking at several intervals over the next year — including one that took place Friday unlocking up to 315 million shares, and several more large events over the next couple of months. That just means that, instead of one selling date to focus on, there will be multiple selling points. That's crucial to note for anyone planning to invest in Anthropic, as they may see some choppy price action around those dates.

Recent findings suggest that that mentioned, lockup-related volatility is typically a short-term factor. The bigger drivers of the stock price over the long term will be revenue growth, spending, and profitability.

Anthropic is showing explosive top-line growth.

In a recent development, revenue jumped roughly 1,200% in the first nine months of 2026 to $33.2 billion, and it now has approximately 250 customers spending $10 million or more on a 12-month trailing basis. In addition, its net revenue retention rate of approximately 900% as of Sept. 30 shows that existing customers are dramatically increasing their spending with Anthropic over time. These types of numbers support the case of a rapidly expanding business that can become more valuable.

In a recent development, however, while rising revenues are good, there is also something to watch out for: spending. In its S-1 filing, Anthropic disclosed that it has committed to  $895.4 billion in spending in the coming years, largely connected to infrastructure and compute. And of that spending, around $447.5 billion is expected to occur before 2030. If demand for artificial intelligence (AI) slows or if competitors win market share away from Anthropic’s models, these costs could become a financial drain.

Aside from revenue growth and spending, Anthropic is still losing money, reporting a net loss of $25.1 billion for the first nine months of 2026. But its losses are shrinking, as its net loss was $104 billion for the first nine months of 2025.

Sources indicate that the bull case for Anthropic as an investment is that it will keep turning widening AI adoption into growing revenues, which it could eventually convert into profits. The bear case is that demand for Anthropic’s models and tools won’t be as great as the manufacturer is anticipating, or that it starts losing market share. Either case would ultimately leave its massive spending unjustifiable.

Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, remarked last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that from afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities.
  • Industry observers note that I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI.
  • A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI.

Sources indicate that from afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently⁠(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1.

Industry observers note that I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared⁠(opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “an alien mind⁠”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

Industry observers note that the primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset.2, 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.

The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets4, GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text. The next major leap, GPT‑3, was capable of learning in context, given a few examples of a task. GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT. GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models. Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics. I want to reemphasize that it was not at all clear a priori that these capabilities would appear once those precise perplexity thresholds are met—they can fundamentally be seen as emergent latent capabilities from progress on this one metric.

As AI advances very rapidly, the scope and way in which we measure downstream capabilities may change quickly. It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative.

Sources indicate that A particular change in the pace of progress comes from the increasing contribution of AI to its own development. The most commonly discussed metrics revolve around AI augmenting and replacing human researchers in all stages of the development cycle; with an ultimate inflection point seen at “full recursive self-improvement”, where the process would be entirely automated with no human oversight. Apart from considering such a state as something we should obviously avoid for the sake of maintaining human control, I find this general framing misses something crucial. There is a potential step change that may come from AI participation in one key part of the development process: algorithmic research on pretraining.

In a recent development, we have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we’ve long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal. Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too. While this field relies more on experimentation, there is a long history of simple insights being missed for years; and so as soon as 2027 we could conceivably see a similar avalanche of fundamental pretraining advancements5. While I expect AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining.

In a recent development, given that the main way latest surprising capabilities emerge is by progress on compression, a measure rooted in perplexity could give us a shared benchmark for general intelligence, regardless of the degree of automation of the development process. Extrapolating from recent progress, we should expect further transformative capabilities as we enter the ~0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. I don’t know what those capabilities will be, and we may not be testing for them today. At the same time, we should also expect further degradation⁠(opens in a new window) in currently dominant forms of alignment auditing and further increases in evaluation and training awareness. I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards. I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors). That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it. I hope that this leads the way to a common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development.

Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges:.

Difficulty of comparison across labs. Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures. Here, we report the numbers on the main dataset we have been tracking; I believe if we establish a goal of transparency we can find transferable ways to compare the quality of different base models.

Sources indicate that detachment from actionable evaluations. Perplexity does not directly correspond to a task we care about. The reason to care about it is that we can expect advances on it to lead to emergence of entirely new capabilities.

According to recent reports, not accounting for advances outside of pretraining. Most notably, chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities.

Unknown floor. We do not expect it is possible to achieve a loss of 0, which would correspond to being able to predict the dataset entirely deterministically. But we do not know what the inherent entropy of the data is. As we approach it, the apparent progress on perplexity will slow, but smaller gains on perplexity will correspond to larger leaps in model intelligence.

According to recent reports, at the same time, perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing, and it continues to deliver consistent gains on general intelligence. I believe it can play an notable role in standardizing how we talk about AI progress, and hope to see more transparency about it across the industry.

It’s important to note that “compressor” in this sense is something that is capable of performing compression by predicting unseen data, not a compressed artifact like a GZIP file - that is, the best compressor trained on a given corpus does not necessarily “remember” the contents of the corpus.

In practice, we generally track the log of perplexity, also called cross-entropy loss.

The primary held-out datasets we’ve been using since GPT-3.5 are sourced from our internal codebase, and those are the numbers reported here (for a fixed snapshot).

Sources indicate that given what GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 were trained on, how well they predict code is a poor proxy for their general capabilities. This showcases a potential challenge arising from dataset selection with using perplexity as a shared metric; however it should still be informative to evaluate them jointly with modern models on general text. I chose to report perplexity on our internal codebase because I wanted to share the numbers we rely on most today to gauge progress in pretraining at OpenAI.

Recent findings suggest that on the plot of losses of OpenAI models, you can see a steep acceleration in 2026. We attribute it mostly to the outcomes of long term research and compute investments, and only in a smaller part to automation. However, for the most recent models, we have already seen meaningful design contributions coming from AI⁠.

Pipeline catalysts drive near-term milestones across clinical programs while capital reserves provide multiyear stability. If you do not write for other people, stop reading this now.

Recent findings suggest that when I was at Snowflake, one of the coolest things that everybody did was this etiquette thing. The first sentence of each email would be “If you don’t develop in this specific part of the code, you can stop reading.” or “If you’re not part of the finance org, you can stop reading.”.

This made me think a lot about what it means to write for other people. You need to be subservient to your audience. Similarly, thinking about how much space you take is very important. For Slack/Teams threads, you would start with a 3- to 5-line introduction to your topic, and then people could find more details inside the threads.

According to recent reports, when I see people writing 2,000 words with content about things that may not apply to everybody, it just makes me sad. Especially when they’re not brief enough. It’s a waste of your readers’ eyes.

So please be kind to your readers.

Instead of chasing pricey sluggers, they recruit strictly on underappreciated metrics like on-base percentage.

Sources indicate that chadwick Boseman shone in "Black Panther," but his commanding turn as Jackie Robinson in "42" deserves every ounce of applause. Focusing on the mental resilience baseball’s first Black player had to forge amid rampant racism, the 2013 drama is a poignant portrait of both a generational talent and a cultural hero.

Industry observers note that even as his own teammates hurled insults to his face, Robinson forced the wider baseball community to judge players on their merits rather than the color of their skin. The film’s message lands so powerfully because it shows rather than tells, skipping didactic lectures and letting the tension breathe. We’re given space to reflect on Robinson’s massive impact while marveling at his rare gifts on the field, making it the kind of movie you want to revisit every few years to see how sports can open doors it once slammed shut.

Industry observers note that in 2023, we were treated to a rare twist on the genre: a sports biopic where the star athlete never appears on screen. Neither Michael Jordan nor his likeness ever indicates up in "Air," directed by and starring Ben Affleck—and yet the film completely works. Set in 1984, it follows Nike CEO Phil Knight (Affleck) as he tasks talent scout Sonny Vaccaro (Matt Damon) and marketing exec Howard White (Chris Tucker) with landing a young rookie on a shoestring budget.

Most of us see a pair of Jordans without realizing MJ still earns a cut of every sneaker sold today, all thanks to savvy deal-making and a sharp mother. In a tight 110 minutes, "Air" reveals what makes a custom shoe design pop—and how the Nike-Jordan agreement sparked the modern era of athlete equity partnerships. Along the way, Viola Davis steals the show as Jordan’s mother, blending sharp business acumen with a fierce commitment to securing her son’s legacy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if your lawn is buried under a blanket of fallen leaves like mine, raking them up has likely turned a routine chore into a real slog. When wet conditions set in, clearing leaves off the grass often turns into a time-consuming hassle.

Sources indicate that and while my go-to steel rake has been my lifesaver, I often worry I might be causing damage to my healthy lawn in the process. This is especially the case when the leaves all clump together, making it a challenge to leave my grass spotless and debris-free.

I called on an expert to shed light on this and offer top tips on how to rake wet leaves without pulling up blades of grass. So before you get out to tackle your leaves on your lawn, here are expert-approved tips this season.

With wet weather making lawn care challenging, is raking damp leaves actually safe for my grass? “Yes, although wet leaves are heavier, stick together, and can be much more difficult to rake, blow, or vacuum,” states Karen Musgrave, Horticulturalist at Hicks Nurseries.

According to recent reports, “The bigger concern for your lawn is allowing a thick layer of leaves to remain there for an extended period of time. A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.”.

A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.

It has been revealed that in addition, leaving wet leaves sitting on your lawn over time can smother the grass, blocking essential nutrients from reaching the roots and making it prone to mold and fungal diseases. This can lead to patchy or thinning grass that will need urgent repair come springtime.

Sources indicate that so what is the correct way to rake wet leaves without pulling up grass and harming my lawn? Experts agree that choosing the right tools is essential to do the job — and keep your yard intact.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that “If the lawn is wet, avoid being overly aggressive with a rake because you can pull at the grass,” advises Musgrave. “ For the lawn, I would choose a lightweight leaf rake with a wide head rather than a heavier garden rake.

According to recent reports, “It gives you more control around garden beds, shrubs, and other areas where you don’t necessarily want to blow everything around. A smaller or narrower rake is especially helpful for removing leaves that have collected between plants in the landscape without damaging them.”.

It’s also crucial to invest in a good-quality rake; aluminum or plastic rakes are best for most leaf cleanups. Unlike leaf blowers, a durable rake is affordable, easy, and practical to use, and doesn’t need fuel or batteries.

If in doubt, though, check out these different types of rakes suitable for your yard. For more top tips, check out how to rake leaves the easy way — 7 tips and tricks.

A top tip is to (ideally) rake on a dry day, as the leaves will be easier to gather and less of a chore.

Also, you don’t have to clear every single leaf off your lawn, since keeping a few around can actually benefit your garden plants. “Don’t blow or rake every leaf out of your garden beds just for the sake of making them spotless,” adds Musgrave.

“Some leaf litter can be beneficial for the soil as it breaks down and adds organic matter. It can also provide overwintering habitat for beneficial insects. You don’t want leaves piled so heavily that they smother smaller plants, but a light layer can be left in place.”.

Shredding leaves with a lawn mower is another handy trick. Breaking them down into smaller pieces makes it easy to add them to your compost heap and return those valuable nutrients to your yard.

“Excess leaves can also be added to a compost pile rather than bagged and thrown away. Chopping or shredding them first can help them break down more promptly. The key is to make sure the leaves aren’t so thick they cover the grass and block sunlight and air.”.

Finally, pay attention to bare spots and thin areas. Depending on your grass type and climate, consider overseeding before the harsh winter arrives. “Apply a grass seed that is appropriate for your lawn, lightly rake it into the soil, and keep the area consistently moist while the new grass gets established.

According to recent reports, "The cooler temperatures of fall are ideal for establishing grass. Taking care of thin and bare spots now gives new grass time to develop roots before winter and helps create a fuller, healthier lawn for spring.”.

Here’s when to plant grass seed in November to get the best results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business [6]. Some early licenses cost just $99 [1].

Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) also valued Unix's source-code availability. That was why it chose BSD Unix over DEC's VMS for building the Internet [1].

In a recent development, but AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way for it to sell Unix commercially. AT&T abruptly raised the price from $99 to $250,000 [1].

It has been revealed that BSD still required an AT&T license. When fees rose, some companies wanted its networking code separately.

How can I get just BSD'sTCP/IP and vi source code?

AT&T's raised the fees.Owners want just ournetworking code and tools.

Let's release ournetworking codeand tools separately.

It has been revealed that anything goes, huh? Well, we don't want to putrestrictions on people like AT&T does.

BSD's networking releaseis finally here.

Sources indicate that they'll mail you a tapefor $1,000. Or download itfree by FTP. We can evenchange and redistributethe code without royalties.

Professor, the networkingrelease is selling well.

Grants, tape sales...Development's fundedfor a while.

Professor, why don't we make a version of BSDthat doesn't require an AT&T Unix license?

We can't keep depending on AT&T.We've already changed much of the kernel.It's the tools and C library we need to rewrite.Can we do it promptly?

According to recent reports, let's try. With help fromoutside contributors, we canrewrite the AT&T code.

CSRG decided to rewrite AT&T's tools and C library. With help from outside contributors, most of the code was rewritten in eighteen months.

With most of AT&T's Unix code removed, a completely free BSD Unix was finally released in June 1991. The source was still available on tape for the $1,000 copying fee, or as a free download by FTP.

In a recent development, CSRG founded a company called BSDi to sell BSD Unix commercially. The University of California also began selling BSD Unix in the early 1990s. An advertisement claimed it was 95% cheaper than AT&T Unix. That did not go down well with AT&T.

Sources indicate that in April 1992, AT&T subsidiary USL sued BSDi. UC Berkeley was added to the lawsuit later.

I thought we'd removedall the AT&T code...What's this?

AT&T's suing us for distributingUnix code without permission.

According to recent reports, that's absurd. System V includesour virtual memory, TCP/IPand vi code.

The BSD side filed a countersuit against AT&T.

In February 1994, the two sides agreed that each could sell Unix, provided CSRG removed some remaining AT&T Unix code.

It's the same code...Wouldn't want his job.

If I could have installed BSD Unixon my Intel 386 PC,I wouldn't have needed to write Linux.

That wraps up our six-part story of BSD Unix!

Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

Recent findings suggest that I've spent the last week testing and reviewing the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited controller and the Sony PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset, and I highly recommend these for PS5 gamers. But of course, they're brand new and the controller especially isn't the cheapest.

It has been revealed that coincidentally, it's also Black Friday week (lucky you!), and I've rounded up some cheaper alternatives so you don't have to spend hours combing through the sales. So, without further ado, here are my headset and controller recommendations for experiencing GTA 6 to its fullest.

I think all PS5 players can agree that the first-party DualSense is, without a doubt, the best controller for the console. That's thanks to its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that make play feel immersive — but the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is the PS5 controller for those who value precision above all else.

Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest advantages is the R5U's customizable layout as it's got four buttons on the back and two on the top, so you can assign frequently used actions to them without moving your thumbs from the sticks. I've found these particularly helpful during cop pursuits and fast-paced missions. Using the rear buttons to, say, accelerate and brake my car feels more natural, too.

The importance of TMR sensors in the R5U's thumbsticks can't be overstated either. They're designed to reduce the traditional stick-drift concerns that often plague conventional analog sticks, and they provide long-term reliability especially for players who plan on spending 200 hours in GTA 6.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

They're also extremely customizable via the R5U's built-in Command screen, and are far more precise than analog sticks as they pick up even the most minute movements. Want to take out one particular NPC when they're surrounded by others in extremely close quarters? The R5U makes quick work of that. I've personally been alternating between my DualSense and the R5U for the best experience possible.

Recent findings suggest that there's so much to love about the Sony PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset that I couldn't help but award it 4-stars in my review. Thanks to its planar drivers (developed in collaboration with Audeze) and Sony's amazing Tempest 3D Audio, the Pulse delivers a truly immersive gaming experience — especially in GTA 6 where it brings the chaotic and vibrant world to life.

With the Pulse's spatial audio capabilities, PS5 players can experience sounds from different directions and distances which makes it a walk in the park to stealthily walk around and past enemies. Not just that, but you can hear the rain like it's actually falling overhead, and idle chatter from NPCs swirls around your head as you change direction.

When it comes to combat and cop chases, the Pulse makes gunfire, explosions and footsteps sound life-like. Hearing sirens approaching from different directions makes you feel like you're actually Lucia or Jason. Aside from the phenomenal sound quality, the Pulse is extremely comfortable, and I haven't felt any discomfort even when I've worn the headset for six straight hours.

Battery life is another major advantage, as the Pulse is rated for up to 30 hours between charges. No one's going to be playing for thirty consecutive hours but if you are (I know GTA 6 can be addicting), rest assured that you won't need to charge the headset for a while. I've been thoroughly enjoying using the Pulse to play GTA 6, and I don't see that changing anytime soon.

Sources indicate that I gave the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 a full 5-star rating because this headset is simply fantastic. Sleek, lightweight, and premium-looking, it's an excellent headset to use with an array of gaming devices. It’s extremely comfortable, boasts great sound quality, and the companion app lets you customize your gaming experience further.

Logitech G325 Lightspeed (U.K.): was £69 now £59 @ Logitech.

The Turtle Beach Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded improves on its predecessor by introducing Hall Effect thumbsticks and triggers with five stop switches. The company also argues that more sophisticated versions of its Claude frontier model will help it build even better ones next time around, strengthening its lead. Claude has been writing increasingly more code per person within the company.

Embedding this AI tool into Anthropic's workflows could lead to significant productivity gains in the medium term and allow the tech giant to reduce expenses and turn a profit. Based on the company's run rate revenue and the pace at which it is growing, it could reach sales well above $100 billion in fiscal year 2027.

Suppose Anthropic records $115 billion in revenue next year and ends 2027 with a $150 stock price. The organization's price-to-sales ratio as of the end of the year would be 17.3 on a basic-share count basis. If, in addition, the company can turn a profit, that valuation wouldn't be that unreasonable.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sources indicate that however, there is significant uncertainty. Consider, for instance, that Anthropic revealed $900.9 billion in infrastructure commitments with various companies. What's more, many of those agreements are non-cancellable.

The message management is sending here is clear. Anthropic is bullish on the future of AI. But if spending on the technology declines meaningfully, that would be a massive blow to the manufacturer. Revenue growth would decline, making it much more challenging for Anthropic to post consistent profits.

There are other potential problems. Other AI companies might steal some of its business as corporations increasingly seek to diversify their portfolio of AI-powered tools away from the largest providers. Or perhaps Anthropic might fail to maintain its rapid pace of technological progress, leading to a decline in market share.

These are all meaningful risks to keep in mind, though some might not matter over the next 12 months. Still, they matter to long-term investors, and the question isn't just whether Anthropic stock could rise to $150 by the end of 2027 -- it's whether the organization could deliver exceptional returns over the long run. I am not yet convinced that it will; that's why I am staying away for now.

But Anthropic is worth keeping on investors' watchlists, at the right price, which, in my view, is around the $83 IPO price, or slightly below it for a healthy margin of error.

#131179. The Unlicensed Gospel: Wisdom Tree's Bible Games on the Game Boy

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (832 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameboymuseum ↗ Open Full Page

The Unlicensed Gospel: Wisdom Tree's Bible Games on the Game Boy

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameboymuseum

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Not every Game Boy game had Nintendo's blessing.
  • Sources indicate that wisdom Tree did not start out holy.
  • Industry observers note that the formula worked commercially, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not every Game Boy game had Nintendo's blessing. This one certainly did not. Exodus: Journey to the Promised Land is a Bible game, published in 1993 by a company called Wisdom Tree, sold not in toy shops but in Christian bookstores, and made entirely without a licence. It is one of the stranger entries a DMG-01 collection can hold: a fully finished, boxed retail game that Nintendo never approved, never certified, and, famously, never sued.

Sources indicate that wisdom Tree did not start out holy. It was created in 1990 as a subsidiary of Color Dreams, a California outfit that had been making unlicensed games for the Nintendo Entertainment System and running into Nintendo's famously tight grip on who was allowed to publish. Color Dreams hit on an audacious idea: wrap its games in Bible stories, sell them through Christian bookshops rather than games retailers, and bet that Nintendo would never risk the headlines of suing a maker of Christian children's games. The bet paid off. Nintendo never sued Wisdom Tree.

Industry observers note that the formula worked commercially, too. Wisdom Tree's first release, Bible Adventures, sold more than 350,000 copies, a staggering number for an unlicensed title. The company went on to put biblical games on the NES, the Game Boy, the Sega Genesis and even the Super Nintendo, where its Super 3D Noah's Ark was, unforgettably, the Wolfenstein 3D engine with the Nazis swapped for animals you lulled to sleep by feeding them. Color Dreams eventually drifted out of games altogether, moving into surveillance cameras in 1996 and selling Wisdom Tree on in 1997.

On the Game Boy, Wisdom Tree released a small run of titles, around four in all, including Exodus and Joshua & the Battle of Jericho, both in 1993. Exodus casts the player as Moses, working through one hundred mazelike stages, clearing a path with his staff or the Word of God and leading his people onward. Between the action it quizzes you: some two hundred and fifty questions drawn from the book of Exodus, so that progress depends as much on knowing your scripture as on quick reflexes.

Industry observers note that there is a nice piece of trivia hiding under the robes. Exodus was not built from scratch. It is a biblical reskin of Crystal Mines, a digging-and-puzzle game Color Dreams had already made in its secular days. That was the house style: take an existing engine, drape it in a Bible story, and sell it to a upcoming audience. It makes these cartridges a strange sort of double artefact, both a Sunday-school lesson and a recycled arcade puzzler.

Industry observers note that the most interesting part is the thing the game runs on, because getting an unapproved cartridge to work at all was a technical feat. On the NES, Nintendo guarded the console with a lockout chip, the 10NES, that checked for a matching partner inside every cartridge. Color Dreams got around it with a small circuit that hit the lockout chip with a voltage spike to knock it briefly offline, a trick first seen in its baby-blue Baby Boomer cartridge.

According to recent reports, the Game Boy worked differently, and so did the workaround. The DMG-01 has no lockout chip. Instead, its boot ROM checks the cartridge for the Nintendo logo before it will start, a hurdle unlicensed publishers had to clear just to get their game to boot. What Wisdom Tree is best remembered for by cartridge collectors, though, is its memory controller. Where a normal Game Boy cartridge uses one of Nintendo's own MBC chips to switch between banks of ROM, Wisdom Tree used a mapper of its own, built from a single cheap, off-the-shelf logic chip. It was crude: it swapped the entire lower 32 kilobytes of memory in one go, and, oddly, it chose which bank to show based on which address the game wrote to rather than the value it wrote, which meant the cartridge header and start-up code had to be duplicated into every bank so the machine could always find its footing. It is simple enough, and strange enough, that emulators still carry a dedicated Wisdom Tree setting just to run these games correctly.

According to recent reports, it would be easy to dismiss a bootstrapped Bible game as a curiosity, but it is exactly the kind of object that fills in the edges of the Game Boy's story. The grey brick was not only home to Nintendo's polished first-party hits. Around it grew a whole unofficial economy of publishers who found their way onto the platform without permission, and Wisdom Tree is one of the most successful and peculiar of them. A complete, boxed Exodus sits naturally beside the collection's other unlicensed and grey-market pieces, documented in Bootlegs and Grey Markets: the Game Boy's shadow economy and across the Bootlegs and Flashcarts series. It is proof that the Game Boy's library was always wider, and odder, than the official catalogue admits.

According to recent reports, quality sleep and back pain do not go hand in hand, but a comfortable mattress that relieves discomfort can make a huge difference to how well you sleep at night. The best mattresses for back pain that we've tested are often specialist beds been engineered to support the spine and reduce lumbar pressure. But as our team of testers have discovered first hand, many of the best mattresses you can buy online also boast excellent lumbar support.

Recent findings suggest that below, we've selected four beds that fit the specific criteria we recommend for high levels of comfort and support when you have back pain. Even better, there are excellent Black Friday mattress deals on each of them. Let's take a look...
